# μεταμόρφωσις

> A static site of in-browser tools for agents: image processing and analysis, PDF, video, audio, maps, tabular
> data, documents, raw bytes. Everything runs in the page on WebAssembly, with WebGPU when the browser has it and
> CPU otherwise. No server, no upload: files never leave the browser. The only thing ever fetched from another
> origin is neural-model weights (from the Hugging Face Hub), and only when a `mind/` tool asks for them.

## How to use it

Open a page, wait for it, call tools:

    await M.ready
    await M.call('sys.rooms')              // the rooms (pages) and what each holds
    await M.call('sys.tools')              // tools of the room you are in
    await M.call('sys.help', {tool: 'pdf.merge'})     // full input schema of one tool
    await M.call('pdf.merge', {inputs: ['a.pdf', 'b.pdf']})

`M.call(name, args)` always resolves to `{ok: true, tool, ms, result}` or `{ok: false, tool, ms, error}`.
The same tools are registered with WebMCP (`document.modelContext`), named with `_` instead of `.` (`pdf_merge`).
The last result is mirrored in the DOM at `script#last-result`; the log is `#log`; previews are painted in `#viewport`.

## Rooms

The tools are split across pages so that no page puts hundreds of tool definitions in your context.
Each room exposes one family plus `fs.*` and `sys.*`. Go to the room that has what you need.

- [image/](image/): raster transforms and filters — convert, resize, crop, blur, edges, morphology, colour
- [analysis/](analysis/): image measurement and forensics — histogram, stats, palette, sharpness, SSIM/PSNR, perceptual hash, FFT, ELA, components, corners, lines, LSB
- [synth/](synth/): synthetic images, dithering, WebGPU playground — noise, fractals, automata, test cards, palettes, custom WGSL shaders
- [vision/](vision/): OCR, barcodes and QR codes, neural image classification
- [pdf/](pdf/): inspect, extract text, render pages, merge, split, rotate, compress, watermark, build from images or markdown
- [video/](video/): probe, convert, compress, trim, frames, contact sheets, GIF, audio extraction
- [audio/](audio/): convert, edit, loudness and spectral stats, spectrogram and waveform images, pitch, tempo, synthesis, DTMF, Morse
- [geo/](geo/): GeoJSON / KML / GPX / TopoJSON / WKT / shapefile conversion, simplify, measure, reproject, render maps
- [data/](data/): CSV / JSON / YAML / TOML / XML / XLSX / Markdown tables — convert, query, stats, schema, diff, charts
- [bytes/](bytes/): identify by magic number, entropy, strings, binary diff, hashes, encodings, zip / tar / gzip
- [doc/](doc/): docx / pptx / epub / html / ipynb / eml to Markdown and back, subtitles, chunking, token estimates, grep, diff
- [mind/](mind/): neural models in the page — `speech.transcribe` (Whisper speech-to-text), `llm.generate` / `llm.chat` (small language models on WebGPU), `model.*` to list, download, cache and unload weights (40 MB – 1.4 GB per model, fetched on demand)
- [claude/](claude/): make any file model-ready — `claude.inspect` tells you what is wrong with a file, `claude.pack` fixes it

A tool from another room still runs if you call it by its full name (its code is loaded on demand); it is just
not listed or offered over WebMCP outside its room.

## When something fails or is slow

- `sys.diag` — what this browser can and cannot do (WebGPU adapter, WASM SIMD, WebCodecs, storage…), with a verdict per room: ok, degraded (and why) or blocked.
- `sys.log {level: 'warn'}` — the page log: every call with duration and backend, downloads, fallbacks, failures, uncaught errors.
- `sys.debug` or `?debug` in the URL — mirror everything to the console.

## Files

Tools read and write a virtual file system by path. It persists in the browser (IndexedDB) across rooms and reloads.

- in: `fs.write {path, text | base64}` (use `append: true` to send a large file in chunks), `fs.fetch {url}` (CORS permitting), or a human drops/pastes a file on the page
- out: `fs.read {path, encoding: text | base64 | dataurl | hex, offset, length}` (256 KiB per call), `fs.download {path}`
- look: `fs.preview {path}` paints the file in `#viewport` — take a screenshot to see it
- manage: `fs.list`, `fs.stat`, `fs.cp`, `fs.mv`, `fs.rm`
- related outputs: every file records `from` (its inputs) and `by` (the tool); `fs.pipelines` groups files into pipelines, `fs.list {pipeline: path}` filters to one

Tools that produce a file return `output: {path, mime, bytes, …}` (or `outputs: [...]`). Pass an `output` argument to
choose the name; otherwise it is derived from the input (`cat.png` → `cat.blur.png`).

## Conventions

- Results are small JSON. Pixels, audio, documents and long text are written to files, never returned inline.
- Tools with a GPU path take `backend: auto | gpu | cpu` and report the backend they used. `sys.env` says what the machine has.
- Heavy engines (ffmpeg, OCR, neural models, PDF renderer) download on first use; the first call is slower.
- Terminal: type `tool key=value …` in `#prompt`; `a | b` pipes a's output file into b; `man <tool>` shows a schema.
  `?x=<command>;<command>` in the URL runs commands at load.

## Machine-readable

- [tools.json](tools.json): every tool of every room with its input schema
